title: Alaska Workshop Part 8: Focus Stacking, Light Mastery, Beams, and Panorama in Photoshop (AK 2-1)

locations.name: Alaska (probable ice cave/glacier site)
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly references an Alaska trip; visuals show glaciers/ice cave features; no exact site coordinates are provided.

summary: This video presents a photographer’s hands-on walkthrough of a full Photoshop/RGB workflow centered on a distinctive, simplified toolset. It covers initial shot evaluation on an Alaska trip, focus-stacking to expand depth of field, and then a detailed post-production process that builds a convincing light source, colors, and depth through layered RAW adjustments, diffusion, color grading, and selective color. The instructor emphasizes practical constraints (e.g., focus-stack imperfections, glacier edges) and demonstrates a mix of time-saving history-based edits, painting with the history brush, clone-stamping for edge alignment, beam creation for architectural light, and panorama stitching with PT GUI, while cautioning about tool choices and the physics of light in landscape scenes like ice caves and glaciers.

sections.title: Intro: workflow philosophy and toolset
sections.description: The presenter lays out a philosophy of working with a small, fixed toolset and a clear visual goal, arguing for a simple, repeatable process rather than learning every Photoshop feature.

sections.title: Foundations of focus stacking and exposure decisions
sections.description: Discussion of focusing strategy, why smaller apertures yield more depth and how to choose exposures for stacking. The speaker emphasizes overlap between frames and explains why some aperture choices (e.g., F9) may fail to resolve all planes.

sections.title: Stack assembly workflow in Photoshop
sections.description: Instructions for bringing stack files into Photoshop, aligning and blending layers, and filling transparencies. The speaker notes limitations and how some elements (like the glacier) may still blur after stacking.

sections.title: Post-stack lighting and zone-based processing
sections.description: Transition to shaping light and color, treating the scene as four processing zones, and using RAW adjustments plus diffusion to create a natural glow and directional lighting that emphasizes the cave opening.

sections.title: Beam creation technique and color refinement
concepts: erasing one side with a larger soft brush
sections.description: Introduction to a specialized technique for creating light beams: precise brush hardness and size, painting beams, then erasing one side to sharpen and intensify, followed by color balancing to integrate beams with the scene.

sections.title: Panorama, stitching, and final compositing
concepts: rule of trapezoids to unsquish top/bottom
sections.description: Discussion of assembling panoramas from multiple shots, adjusting exposure to match frames, addressing distortions with trapezoid rules, and using warp tools to create believable wide views; includes mirroring for sphere stitching and final crop decisions.

History brush usage to apply previous steps

Panorama stitching in PT GUI; exposure matching
